issues.failure_explanation: The comparability |b_j|^2 = (\int_\gamma |w-q_j|^{-2k-2}|dw|)^{-1} \simeq d(q_j)^{2k+1} holds only for source points within bounded distance of \gamma. For exterior points with d(q) -> \infty, \int_\gamma |w-q|^{-2k-2}|dw| \simeq |\gamma| d^{-2k-2}, so |b|^2 \simeq d^{2k+2}. Such normalized wavelets tend to unimodular constants divided by |\gamma|^{1/2}, so |(f,\psi_j^+)| \simeq |\int_\gamma f\,|dw|| / |\gamma|^{1/2}. A Whitney set for all of \Omega^- has about \varepsilon^{-2} points in each dyadic annulus, hence infinitely many far points. Therefore \sum_j |(1,\psi_j^+)|^2 = \infty and the upper frame bound fails for f = 1. The 'analogous' exterior case of the discretization estimate is false, so the delta = infinity case of the theorem is false. The delta < infinity proof adds infinitely many far points p_j^-, invokes the false delta = infinity case to obtain a frame, and then removes those points. Its premise is therefore false.

failure_location.quote: the other case, where $+$ is replaced by $-$, and vice versa, is analogous.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the theorem to delta < infinity, or require exterior source points to lie in a bounded set. Then give a new direct discretization proof for bounded Whitney sets, where |b_j|^2 \simeq d^{2k+1} holds with delta-dependent constants. This proof must use the square function estimate on \Omega_\delta^\pm, and it must handle the lower bound via Poincare-Wirtinger and the Caccioppoli-type lemma, even though d(z) differs from dist(z, \partial\Omega_\delta). The reduction to delta = infinity must be abandoned.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is false for delta = infinity on the exterior side. The delta < infinity case, which the numerics use, is left without a valid proof. The Hardy-space frame property (Prop. frames_for_hardy_spaces), and the intro and abstract claims built on it, become unsupported.
issues.title: Lusin frame upper bound fails for unbounded exterior Whitney sets (delta = infinity); the delta < infinity reduction collapses
issues.why_classification: A stated regime (delta = infinity) is false and must be excluded. The proof strategy for the remaining regime depends on it, so a replacement argument for the main theorem is required.

issues.failure_explanation: For a bi-Lipschitz map of R^n with constant L, Lebesgue measure scales by at most L^n, so m(\rho(E)) >= L^{-n} m(E), not L^{-1} m(E). For n >= 2 and L > 1 the stated inequality is false. The derived bound m(\rho(E_j)) >= m(B_j')/(L^{3n+1}\sigma), and hence the stated covering constant N <= 4^n L^{3n+1}\sigma, are not established. The correct argument gives 4^n L^{4n}\sigma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace L by L^n in the measure estimates and state N <= 4^n L^{4n} \sigma.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative covering-constant bound in the lemma is wrong. The qualitative Whitney-set conclusion, used for Example explicit_whitney_partition, survives.
issues.title: Wrong measure distortion under bi-Lipschitz maps invalidates the stated covering-constant bound
issues.why_classification: A local constant correction. The finiteness of the covering constant and all downstream uses are unaffected.
